steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The age of criminal responsibility in England and Wales is 10 — one of the lowest in Europe. In Scotland it was raised to 12 in 2021 (from 8). Many argue it should be raised to 14.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Children aged 10-17 are dealt with in youth courts, not adult courts. Youth courts are less formal: no public gallery, judges don't wear wigs, parents must attend, and reporting restrictions protect the young person's identity.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Young offenders can receive: Referral Orders (first offence, attend a youth offender panel), Youth Rehabilitation Orders (community sentence with requirements), or Detention and Training Orders (custodial, from age 12).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: ASSET assessments identify the needs of young offenders and the factors contributing to their offending behaviour — such as family problems, education, substance misuse, and mental health.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always specify which part of the UK you are referring to — ages differ between England, Scotland, and NI When evaluating the youth justice system, balance welfare (rehabilitation) vs justice (accountability) Use specific examples of youth sentences — Referral Orders, YROs — not just general statements
